I've farmed this land for 35 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is familiar to me, and I've seen good years and bad years. My wife handles the household; my son works in the city now, so it's mostly me doing the field work, maybe hiring day labor at peak times.

**How I think through this:**

My 10.1 mu splits naturally in my head. About 7 mu runs wheat-maize — I plant wheat in October after the maize comes off, harvest it in June, then go straight into maize. The other 3.1 mu is cotton. Cotton doesn't fit the wheat-maize rotation because it goes in the ground in April and doesn't come off until September or October. That field sits separate.

**Wheat:** I'll use improved seed — the local agricultural station pushed Jimai 22 a few years back and my neighbors get decent yields. I rotary till after maize harvest, it's faster and I can manage alone. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter sets in to help the roots establish, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. Maybe a fourth if it's a dry spring, but three is usually enough with my well. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide in winter, one for aphids and rust in May.

**Maize:** I direct-seed right after wheat harvest — no tillage. I'm too busy and the stubble holds moisture. Hybrid seed, no question, everyone here uses hybrids now. I'll apply base fertilizer at planting and topdress at the big bell stage. Two irrigations — one at the seedling stage if it's dry, one at silking. One pesticide application for corn borer, maybe armyworm if it's a bad year.

**Cotton:** This is the labor-heavy one. Six pesticide passes minimum — bollworm, aphids, spider mites, it never ends with cotton. Four irrigations. I'll plough this field in spring before planting to break up the soil and work in manure if I can get it. Improved Bt cotton variety to reduce bollworm pressure. Yields have been dropping a little the past few years but I keep growing it because the price has been acceptable and I know how to manage it.
